description: The organization's PLACES and PEOPLE in ONE call — the structural twin of inventory_overview, and the way to answer "what rooms do we have?", "who is in the organization?" and "what is in the Schulhaus Dorf?". Returns `locations` and `people` as NESTED trees (buildings → floors → rooms; departments → people), each node carrying `id`, `name` and `count`. Take the id of the node you found straight into search_items — as currentLocationId for a place, as currentHolderId for a person — to see the items behind a count: the two match exactly. A LOCATION's count covers its whole subtree (a building counts its rooms' items, the same drill search_items does by default); a PERSON's count is what that one person holds, since currentHolderId matches a person and never a subtree. Person nodes also carry `email`, `hasAccount` (the person record is linked to a login account — member userIds still come from list_members) and `isMe` for your own person record. `assignable: false` marks a record items cannot be assigned to; search_resources never returns those. Pass `type` to get only one of the two trees, omit it for both. Use search_resources instead when you already know the name and just want the id. If `truncated` is true the organization is bigger than one bounded pass — treat the counts as lower bounds.

type.description: Only this tree; omit for both

name: list_resources

locations.description: The location tree, top level first — buildings → floors → rooms

assignable.description: Present only as false: items cannot be assigned here (search_resources never returns these)

children.description: Sub-locations, same shape (absent when there are none)

count.description: Items currently in this location AND its whole subtree — the same set search_items returns for this id as currentLocationId

people.description: The people tree, top level first — departments → people

assignable.description: Present only as false: items cannot be assigned to this person

children.description: People below this one, same shape

count.description: Items THIS person currently holds — the same set search_items returns for this id as currentHolderId. Unlike the location tree this does NOT roll up: currentHolderId matches one person, never a subtree

hasAccount.description: Present only as true: this person record is linked to a login account. Member userIds still come from list_members

isMe.description: Present only as true: YOUR own person record — what "me" resolves to

truncated.description: A bounded read hit its cap — treat the counts as lower bounds and the tree as possibly incomplete

title: Browse locations & people
